subject: Discovery: multi-tenant controls, quotas & routing — recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps from today's multi-tenant controls discussion

Hi Emily & Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed path forward so we stay aligned.

What we heard (pain points):
- Per-customer burst handling: you need predictable SLAs for critical tenants during scheduled peak windows.
- Fairness & isolation: preventing noisy tenants from impacting others (rate/priority controls).
- Billing attribution: token-level cost breakdown and per-tenant usage reporting.
- Security/compliance: ability to host within a VPC and provide audit logs for KMS and token usage.

Current stack notes you shared:
- Primary app hosted on AWS (us-west-2).
- Inference currently backed by a single shared endpoint (internal autoscaling, some custom throttles).
- Logging/metrics via Datadog; billing aggregated in Snowflake.

Success criteria (what would make this a win):
1) 99th percentile latency < 400ms for high-tier tenants at our peak payloads.
2) Per-tenant soft quotas with hard caps and rate-tier escalation.
3) Clear cost attribution (per-tenant tokens + summary export).
4) Ability to route requests by tenant to different model variants (eg. small/large) for cost controls.

Recommended next steps:
- I'll share a short overview doc that maps Redwood's multi-tenant controls to each success criterion (attached).
- Schedule a technical call with our Solutions Engineer (Ava) to validate proposed rate/table configs and a sample rollout plan (30–45m).
- If procurement is interested, we can circulate a draft SLA/commit that reflects the tiering guarantees (attached draft).

Questions we still have for you before the tech call:
- Typical request distribution (p50/p95 token length) and expected peak qps per high-tier tenant?
- Are there existing legal/contract constraints around data residency that would require Private deployment?

Proposed dates for a technical follow-up: Nov 3 or Nov 5 (US mornings). Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Hi Marcus —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- For p95 payloads we're typically ~600 tokens; p50 ~120 tokens. Peak for our two largest tenants is roughly 45–60 rps each during scheduled events.
- We require per-tenant usage reports daily and CSV exports to our billing bucket.
- We prefer to avoid an on-prem/private deployment unless strictly necessary; VPC + cross-account logs should be fine for now.

Procurement (cc'd) will review the SLA draft and follow up separately with any contractual questions.

Two quick asks before the tech call: can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-tenant model pinning (so Tenant A always routes to GPT-large-v2 while Tenant B uses a quantized small model) and whether you have examples of throttling policies we can review?

Nov 3 works for Tom and me — morning PT is ideal.

Thanks,

Thanks Emily — great detail, exactly what we need. Answers inline below.

Per-tenant model pinning:
- Yes. We support tenant-scoped routing rules that can pin a tenant to an explicit model variant or route by policy (e.g., by cost tier, latency SLO, or custom attribute). Routing is declarative in the config so you can change pinning without redeploying code.

Throttling policies / example:
- Soft quota: notify at 80% usage (configurable window), grace bursts up to 2x baseline.
- Hard cap: enforced at the token or request level with HTTP 429.
- Priority queuing: high-tier tenants can be assigned a higher priority class that preempts background/low-priority traffic.
- Adaptive scaling fallback: when capacity constrained we can route low-tier tenants to a cheaper model variant automatically.

What I'll bring to the technical call: a proposed per-tenant rate table based on the numbers you provided, an example policy file showing pinning + priority classes, and a sample billing CSV layout. I've attached the controls overview and a draft SLA for procurement to review.

Tech call attendees we suggest: Ava (Solutions Eng) + Neha (Tech Partnerships) from our side; Emily + Tom + one infra engineer from Acme.

I've booked a tentative slot Nov 3 09:30 PT; can you confirm and I'll send the calendar invite.

Best,
Marcus
